rules.sentence: Injuries to the anterior interosseous nerve resulting from direct external trauma do not meet the diagnostic criteria for anterior interosseous nerve syndrome.[6]
Only spontaneous cases presenting with weakness of the muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve qualify as true anterior interosseous nerve syndrome.

Electrodiagnostic studies in many patients with anterior interosseous nerve syndrome reveal a more widespread median motor involvement extending beyond the muscles specifically innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve.[7]
The most frequently identified cause involves an idiopathic immune-mediated neuritis.
An intrinsic compressive lesion in the forearm, including conditions such as compartment syndrome and localized compression neuropathy, represents the second most common etiology.[8][7]
